title: Groupe de Galois motivique : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: section (4), titled "Double visage", of a list of candidate fully faithful realisation functors on motives. The previous page had treated (2) l-adic Galois realisations via Tate, and (3) de Rham with Gauss–Manin plus Betti with comparison, assuming Hodge and using Griffiths.

Setup. Take S = Spec k with k algebraic over Q. To a motive M attach the triple (T_DR(M), T_B(M), phi_M), where phi_M is the comparison T_B(M) ⊗_Q C ≅ T_DR(M) ⊗_k C. Deliberately, no Hodge filtration on T_DR and no Hodge structure on T_B are kept. In modern terms this is the 'de Rham–Betti realisation' into the category of triples (Q̄-vector space, Q-vector space, C-isomorphism). The question is whether this functor is fully faithful.

Step 1. By Galois descent one reduces to k = Q̄.

Step 2. Viewing T_DR(M) as a Q̄-subspace of T_B(M) ⊗ C, the data is equivalent to (T_B(M), sigma). Here sigma is the canonical descent datum ('stratification') of T_B ⊗ C relative to C/Q̄. Grothendieck's word reads like 'connexion'; it is consistent with the stratification language of the previous page. T_DR is the set of 'horizontal' (descended) elements, so sigma and T_DR determine each other.

Step 3 (torsor formulation). Let G = Aut^⊗(T_B) on the finitely generated ⊗-subcategory of Mot(Q̄) generated by M; this is the motivic Galois group, a Q-group.
- The comparison isomorphisms are a point of the torsor Isom^⊗(T_B ⊗ Q̄, T_DR). Since Q̄ is algebraically closed this torsor is trivial.
- So the data is a single 'period point' g ∈ G(C)/G(Q̄).
- For every G-module V (= Betti realisation of a motive), T_DR = g(V_Q̄) ⊂ V ⊗_Q C.

Step 4. By rigidity, Hom(M,N) = Hom(1, M^∨ ⊗ N), so full faithfulness reduces to unit-Homs.
- Motivic side: V^G.
- Target side: rational Betti vectors that are de Rham-rational, V ∩ g(V̄) with V̄ = V ⊗ Q̄.
- The question becomes: is the inclusion V^G ⊂ V ∩ g(V̄) an equality for all V?
- One may assume V simple. If dim V = 1, V is a Tate twist Q(n) (a rank-one Q-Hodge structure is of type (p,p)). Then V ∩ g(V̄) ≠ 0 forces (2πi)^n ∈ Q̄, so n = 0 by Lindemann. 'ça marche'.

Step 5 (next page, completing the thread).
- Let T̄ be the Q̄-Zariski closure of g.
- If x ∈ V with g^{-1}x = y ∈ V̄, the Q̄-defined condition h^{-1}x = y holds on all of T̄. So s t^{-1} fixes x for s, t ∈ T̄, and the group H generated by T̄T̄^{-1} lies in the stabiliser G_x.
- Hence if H = G, which holds when g is Q̄-generic, i.e. under Grothendieck's period conjecture, the functor is fully faithful.
- More sharply, it suffices that H contain a Borel subgroup. For connected G, V^B = V^G because the orbit map G/B → V from a projective variety to an affine space is constant. This explains the marginal 'NB Connexe': the motivic group over Q̄ is expected to be connected.
- A margin points to CM abelian varieties and elliptic curves as test cases.
errors: The identification of sigma as a 'connexion' is loose. On a point Spec Q̄ the correct notion is a Q̄-structure, i.e. a descent datum/stratification relative to C/Q̄. The argument is unaffected.
The 'si V est...' sentence is garbled and partially duplicated in the manuscript. The intended statement, T_DR = g(V_Q̄) for every G-module V, is correct.
The dimension-1 case silently assumes rank-one motives over Q̄ are Tate twists. This is true for Hodge-theoretic reasons, given the standard conjectures on the semisimplicity/description of motives.
Connectedness of G (needed for the Borel criterion on the next page) is only flagged ('NB Connexe'), not proved. It is conjectural for motives over Q̄ (known for absolute Hodge/motivated versions).

ideas.what: Question whether the Betti + algebraic de Rham + comparison realisation, without Hodge filtration, is fully faithful on motives over number fields / Q̄
ideas.modern_name: de Rham–Betti realisation / de Rham–Betti classes conjecture (weak Grothendieck period conjecture)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Y. André (Une introduction aux motifs, 2004, §7.5); Bost–Charles (2016) 'de Rham–Betti classes'
ideas.where_published: Not as such. The period conjecture appears only as a footnote in 'On the de Rham cohomology of algebraic varieties' (1966) and via Lang's 1966 book.

ideas.what: Comparison data over Q̄ encoded as a period point g ∈ G(C)/G(Q̄) of the motivic Galois group, with T_DR(V) = g(V_Q̄)
ideas.modern_name: period torsor Isom^⊗(ω_dR, ω_B), torsor form of the period conjecture

ideas.what: Reduction of full faithfulness to the equality V^G = V ∩ g(V̄) for all representations V; rank-one case via transcendence of π
ideas.usually_credited_to: André; Bost–Charles (divisors on abelian varieties via Wüstholz)

ideas.what: (next page) Stabiliser argument: the Q̄-Zariski closure of g generates a subgroup fixing de Rham-rational Betti vectors. Hence the period conjecture implies full faithfulness, and it suffices that this subgroup contain a Borel (V^B = V^G for connected G)
ideas.modern_name: period conjecture ⇒ de Rham–Betti full faithfulness; Borel fixed-point criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: André / Bost–Charles for the implication; the Borel refinement unsure

missed.claim: Grothendieck himself formulated, c. 1965, the full-faithfulness question for the de Rham–Betti realisation without Hodge filtration. He cast it in Tannakian form: a period point g ∈ G(C)/G(Q̄) with de Rham lattice g(V_Q̄), reducing the question to V^G = V ∩ g(V̄). The literature usually attributes this torsor/Galois reformulation and the 'de Rham–Betti' conjecture to André and later Bost–Charles. Grothendieck's own published trace is only the transcendence-degree footnote.
missed.quote: la donnée de g∈G(C)/G(Q̄) ... T_DR(M) n'est autre que le Q̄-visage g(V_Q̄)⊂V⊗_Q C. Donc la question est simplement si pour tout V, l'inclusion V^G ⊂ V∩g(V̄) est une identité.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: it shows the period torsor and the de Rham–Betti conjecture in Grothendieck's motivic Galois notes, earlier than usually documented.

missed.claim: A criterion weaker than Zariski density of the period point is sketched (continued on the next page). It suffices that the group generated by T̄T̄^{-1} contain a Borel subgroup of the connected motivic group. This intermediate transcendence condition is not, to my knowledge, isolated in the literature.
missed.quote: NB Connexe ... [S'il est de dim. 1, c'est une puissance du Tate et ça marche]
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Gives a possibly more tractable sufficient condition for de Rham–Betti full faithfulness. It would sit between known partial results (Wüstholz-based, e.g. Bost–Charles) and the full period conjecture.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics is now standard (de Rham–Betti realisation, period torsor). But finding Grothendieck already phrasing it in 1965 via the motivic Galois group, a period point mod G(Q̄), and invariants is a notable unpublished precursor of André's and Bost–Charles's formulations. The Borel refinement on the next page adds a small extra.

'catégorie de type fini de la catégorie Mot(k)' should read 'sous-catégorie ⊗ de type fini engendrée par M dans Mot(k)'.
The phrase 'pour tout V, l'' is duplicated; it belongs only to 'Donc la question est simplement si pour tout V, l'inclusion'.
The struck-out line at the bottom reads '[-Je reviens au cas de-]'. The bracket closing 'ça marche' ends the nested remark.
